exposure: single-layered unlocked closure of their uterine incision during their first cesarean delivery
double-layered unlocked closure of their uterine incision during their first cesarean delivery
cohort: 280 women undergoing their first cesarean delivery
finding: There was no significant difference in the size of the uterine scar defect, as assessed by saline infusion sonography 3 months postoperatively, between single- and double-layered uterine incision closure techniques.
mod_finding: This study found no significant difference in the size of the cesarean scar defect three months postpartum between single- and double-layered closure of the uterine incision during a cesarean delivery.
